model: YVAA / YVFA / YAGK Chiller, YT3 panel (SC-EQ)
equipment_type: Air-cooled variable-speed screw chiller (via SC-EQ card)
applies_to: YORK YVAA, YVFA (free cooling) and YAGK air-cooled variable-speed screw chillers (two refrigerant systems) fitted with the SC-EQ communication card and the YT3 control panel.
summary: YVAA, YVFA and YAGK chillers connect to a BAS through the SC-EQ communication card on BACnet MS/TP (or Modbus RTU / N2). The BAS can start/stop the chiller, write the cooling setpoint, current limit and sound limit, and inhibit the free cooling valve. Read-only points cover chilled liquid and ambient temperatures, per-system pressures, temperatures, % FLA, kW and lockouts, VSD values, condenser fan data, free cooling (YVFA) values, and multistate operational, fault and warning codes per system. This is the list for units with the YT3 control panel.
notes: Access is inferred: the sheet has no read/write column. The remote block (AV 1, AV 2, AV 3, BV 1, BV 2, BV 3) is treated as commandable and MV 65001 as writable; everything else as read-only.
AV 37 and AV 42 mean subcooling on microchannel condensers and evaporator level on round-tube condensers; they are merged into one row each.
Free cooling points (BV 35, BV 40-41, AV 48-54, MV 12, AV 450) only apply to YVFA units with free cooling enabled; condenser fan points depend on the fan control type.
Operational, fault and warning code MVs (MV 1-4, MV 15-16) use the Status Codes tables + 1, as the sheet says to add 1 for BACnet MSV values; the AV copies (AV 417-418, AV 501-504) use the raw code.
The sheet also lists a Total Run Hours value (sum of both systems) with no BACnet object; it is left out.

Multistate states with their own enum in the points table (Units, system state, free cooling mode) are shown as printed, from 0. BACnet multistate values start at 1, so the device may report the printed number + 1; confirm by discovery.
Units shown are the IP units; with MV 65001 set to SI the card reports °C, bar and so on. Spare and reserved objects are left out.

source.title: YVAA / YVFA / YAGK (YT3) SC-EQ BAS Points List

integration.summary: Put the chiller in remote control (BV 20 reads Remote), then start/stop it with BV 1 and write the cooling setpoint (AV 1) and current limit (AV 2). Read BV 5 for chiller run, the leaving chilled liquid temperature and VSD frequency, BV 6 for the chiller alarm and the per-system fault codes for the cause.

minimum_points.name: LOCAL REMOTE CONTROL MODE
minimum_points.why: Must read Remote (1) for BMS control

integration.enable: BV 20 shows Local or Remote control mode. The points list gives no point to change it and no write-enable point.
integration.heartbeat: The operational code list includes 'Loss of External Communications'; the sheet gives no timeout or heartbeat point.
setup: The BAS connects to the SC-EQ J12 port (RS-485: +, -, COM/REF, SHLD). The card detects BACnet MS/TP, Modbus RTU or N2 and the baud rate by itself; allow up to 120 seconds after power-up.
The MAC address (1-127) is set on DIP switch SW1 (switch 8 unused). Cycle the card's power after changing it.

The device instance defaults to 5000 + the MAC address (MAC 6 gives 5006). To use another number, set Device Instance Mode to Manual and enter the instance with the SC-AP / MAP tool, or write BV 65000 (mode) and AV 65000 (instance ID).
MV 65001 Units sets whether the BAS sees IP or SI values, independent of the chiller display; set it to match the chiller.
gotchas: The remote (commandable) setpoints read as unreliable until the BAS writes them the first time.
The SC-EQ only exposes the points that apply to the chiller it detects; if it replaces an E-Link, re-discover the device so old non-applicable points don't sit offline.
Fault/inhibit codes are per refrigerant system (MV 2, MV 4); there is no single unit fault code, so alarm on BV 6 and read both.
